Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (3dLME) with familywise error whole-brain correction and cluster thresholds, and voxelwise results/coordinates are described in text/figures/tables. Relevant details (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing and statistical software: SPM12, AFNI, FSL, BioImage Suite) are reported. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an fMRI cue-reactivity investigation using visual (and tactile) cannabis cues, so it meets I3. It also performed within-subject contrasts of cannabis vs neutral cues within its PPI connectivity analyses, satisfying I4. However, the paper does not report any qualifying task-evoked voxelwise activation contrasts (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) of drug cues > control stimuli; instead the main reported results are seed-based connectivity (PPI) and Granger effective-connectivity analyses. According to exclusion criterion E4 (studies that report only seed-based connectivity/effective connectivity without also reporting a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result), this study must be excluded. Inclusion I5 (a qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked activation result) is not met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual smoking cues (No Smoking Signs, smoking symbols) in human smokers that directly addresses the review objective. It includes within-participant contrasts of cigarette cues versus control stimuli (e.g., SSs/NSSs - CSs/CNSs and related ANOVA contrasts) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results (a within-participant two-way ANOVA with clusterwise familywise-error correction reported). The main text presents voxelwise results (significant clusters/regions) and refers to supplementary materials for details. Participant characteristics (male smokers, sample sizes) and cue types are reported; some preferred details (e.g., MRI field strength) are not explicit in the excerpt but that is not exclusionary. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only analyses, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion.

This manuscript is a protocol/experimental design paper reporting planned fMRI cue-reactivity methods but no reported empirical voxelwise results. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI cue-reactivity using visual heroin-related stimuli) and I4 (a within-participant drug-cue > neutral contrast is specified). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results are reported in the paper), I6 (no voxelwise results available in text/tables/supplement), I7 (participant demographics not reported). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (non-empirical manuscript without original human fMRI results). Because the paper lacks reported group-level voxelwise task-evoked results, it does not provide the required data for the meta-analysis and must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual word cues (alcohol-related vs neutral words), with within-subject contrasts (alcohol>neutral) and group-level voxelwise analyses reported across the whole brain (cluster- and voxel-level thresholds described). Participant demographics and scanning/preprocessing details are provided and the manuscript includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual drug cues (heroin/prescription opioid images) and other visual stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts of drug>neutral and group-level voxelwise analyses (whole-brain regression with TFCE cluster-level correction) as well as ROI analyses; results are reported in the main text and figures/tables. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (SPM12), task design, and participant/sample info are provided. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (palatable food images) and a within-participant contrast (food > nonfood). The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (one-sample t-tests and whole-brain multiple regression with cluster-level FWE correction) with coordinates and figures, and provides MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical details (3T, SPM12). Thus it meets all stated inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplementary material not required for inclusion.

Exclusion criterion met: E3 (study reports only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected result). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (multimodal audiovisual cue paradigm includes a visual cue component), I4 (within-participant contrast of cocaine cues > neutral control segments was computed), I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing details are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected statistical maps or coordinate tables are reported for a task-evoked voxelwise analysis), I6 (no qualifying voxelwise results are available in tables/figures as group-level voxelwise coordinates). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded for failing I5 and meeting E3.

Exclusion E3 met: the study reports only ROI-based analyses (activation extracted from a nucleus accumbens mask using 3dROIstats and LME models) and does not present any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity with clear visual cues—MID task cues), I4 (within-participant contrast gain $5 > gain $0), and I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistics). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group-level results reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded for failing to meet I5 / meeting E3.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol and neutral images (and stress images) as cue stimuli, reporting within-participant contrasts (alcohol>neutral, stress>neutral, A-N, S-N) and whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses with family-wise error cluster correction (AFNI, voxel p<0.001, FWE cluster α<0.05). Participant demographics (age/sex), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, details in supplement) are reported. Results are presented in figures and supplemental tables. Therefore all inclusion criteria for task-evoked visual cue-reactivity voxelwise results are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual cannabis and cigarette images (visual cues). Within-participant contrasts of interest are reported (Can > Neutral and Can > Neutral + Cigarette). The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked analyses (exploratory whole-brain 2x2 ANOVAs with FEAT, cluster-wise correction Z>2.3, cluster p<.05). Demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (fMRIPrep, FSL/FEAT) are reported. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol-related pictures) and neutral controls. It includes within-participant contrasts of alcohol-associated pictures > neutral pictures (cue exposure task) and reports voxelwise group-level task-evoked statistical results (whole-brain fixed-effects analyses with cluster thresholds and Talairach coordinates, Bonferroni correction). Voxelwise results are presented in tables/figures with coordinates. The manuscript reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), cue type, and preprocessing/statistical software (Turbo-BrainVoyager, BrainVoyager, SPSS). All inclusion criteria I3–I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity with a within-subject alcohol>water (drug cue>control) contrast and whole-brain cluster-corrected voxelwise results. Although primary stimulus modality is gustatory (taste), the task includes an explicit visual cue component (visual presentation of “Alcohol Taste”/“Control Taste”) making it a multimodal design that includes visual cues. The paper reports whole-brain cluster-corrected analyses with tables of peak coordinates, and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL). Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text.

This fMRI cue-reactivity study used multimodal (audio + picture) personalized cues, and performed within-participant contrasts (e.g., cannabis vs neutral) for subjective craving and for seed-to-seed ROI functional connectivity. However, the paper does not report any group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected). All neuroimaging results described are ROI/seed-to-seed connectivity analyses rather than voxelwise activation maps or SVC-corrected task-evoked contrasts. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and must be excluded. Exclusion IDs: E3 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise result) and E4 (seed-based connectivity without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result). Inclusion IDs met: I3 (visual component present), I4 (within-participant drug cue>control contrasts were performed, albeit for connectivity measures), I7 (reporting of participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing software). Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise task-evoked results). Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it reports only ROI-based task analyses and does not provide a qualifying group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked result (Exclusion E3). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI cue-reactivity using visual cocaine and other evocative images), I4 (within-participant contrasts: cocaine vs neutral were defined and analyzed), I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criterion NOT met: I5 (no whole-brain voxelwise or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise results are presented; analyses are ROI extractions and ROI-wise ANOVAs). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore excluded under E3.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual film cues (cocaine, sex, nature) that assesses cue-induced craving. It includes within-subject contrasts (cocaine film > nature film) and group-level voxelwise, task-evoked statistical analyses (one-sample and two-sample t tests with voxel-wise thresholds and cluster extent) reported across the whole brain and summarized in tables/figures. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI v2.2) are reported. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (pictures) to probe cue-reactivity and neurofeedback effects. It reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol cues > rest/control and uses group-level voxelwise statistical analyses: FWE-corrected whole-brain results (right inferior frontal gyrus) and small-volume-corrected ROI results in the ventral striatum, with peak MNI coordinates provided. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, Turbo-BrainVoyager) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of opioid cue-reactivity using an opioid-word Stroop task (visual word cues). It reports within-participant contrasts of opioid words versus neutral words (OW minus NW) and conducts group-level voxelwise SPM12 second-level analyses (one-sample and two-sample t-tests) with cluster-level FWE-corrected results, satisfying the requirement for a task-evoked voxelwise result. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (SPM12, AFNI steps), and participant demographics/age range. Although the paper also reports DCM effective connectivity results, it includes the requisite voxelwise activation analyses, so it is eligible for inclusion in a meta-analysis of visual drug-cue reactivity.

This paper reports task-based perfusion fMRI in human smokers using audiovisual smoking cues (visual component present). It includes within-participant contrasts of smoking cues > nonsmoking (cue vs control) at the group level, and reports voxelwise whole-brain statistical results with MNI coordinates, cluster thresholds, tables, and figures. Methods (imaging, stimuli, preprocessing/statistics) and participant demographics are described. Thus it satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for visual cue fMRI task-evoked voxelwise results and related reporting. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of cue-reactivity using visual cocaine cue videotapes (clear visual component). The paper reports within-participant contrasts comparing cocaine-cue viewing (first 30 s and full 3 min) to a neutral baseline and conducts group-level voxelwise analyses (whole-brain voxelwise correlations with TES and group-level voxelwise comparisons relapsers vs nonrelapsers), reporting cluster coordinates and significance thresholds. MRI field strength (1.5 T), participant age/sex, cue type, and preprocessing/statistical approaches are described. The full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for visual cue-reactivity, within-participant cue>control contrasts, and reporting of whole-brain voxelwise group-level task-evoked results (coordinates and thresholds). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without within-subject contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual cannabis cues (images) and reports within-participant contrasts (cannabis > neutral). The paper presents group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses: exploratory ROI voxelwise analyses using FLAME produced a significant cluster in the left putamen with MNI coordinates (i.e., a small-volume/ROI-corrected voxelwise result). Methods report participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT/FLAME). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria. Results suitable for meta-analysis (coordinate reported).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual cocaine-related cues (cocaine pictures) vs natural scene control pictures with a within-participant contrast (cocaine>natural). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical analyses are reported (whole-brain inference: height threshold Z>3 and cluster probability p<.05, corrected for whole-brain multiple comparisons), with VBM and fMRI voxelwise results and seed coordinates (MNI) provided. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Given these facts, the study meets all inclusion criteria for cue-reactivity fMRI meta-analysis and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images of alcoholic vs. non-alcoholic beverages). It includes a within-subject contrast 'Alcohol – Non-Alcohol' (I4) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses using FSL Randomise with TFCE and permutation testing, presenting significant clusters and MNI coordinates (I5, I6). The study clearly reports participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer, SPM2, FSL) (I7). It therefore meets I3–I7. No exclusion criteria apply: it is not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity-only (E4), includes the required within-participant cue>control contrast rather than only between-group contrasts (E5), and is empirical human fMRI data (not E6). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses and explicitly states that a voxelwise approach was not completed, thus meeting exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual cannabis cue-reactivity task) and I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no clear within-participant drug-cue > control within-subject contrast is reported) and I5 (no group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study used an MIDT with monetary reward outcomes (dollar/cent/no-money) and modeled outcome onsets rather than visual cue onsets; it therefore does not present within-participant cue>control contrasts relevant to drug or natural reward cue-reactivity. Specifically, the paper lacks analyses of drug-cues>control or natural-reward-cues>control (I4 not met) and does not constitute a cue-reactivity design with visual cue contrasts (I3 not met). The study does report group-level voxelwise whole-brain results (satisfies I5), presents voxelwise findings in figures/tables (I6), and reports participant demographics and MRI/preprocessing details (I7). However, because it does not include the required within-participant cue>control contrast, it meets exclusion criterion E5 (absence of an accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses and does not present any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results. Exclusion criterion met: E3. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study uses visual drinking cues/multimodal design including visual cues), I4 (within-participant contrast of drinking cues > neutral/control cues was performed), I7 (participant demographics and acquisition/preprocessing details are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise result is reported). Full text appears complete, and the exclusion is based on analytic reporting (ROI-only) relative to the meta-analysis requirement for voxelwise results.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study in treatment-seeking cigarette smokers using a visual smoking-cue paradigm (with handling/smelling; multimodal but includes visual images). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of smoking cues > neutral cues and presents group-level voxelwise whole-brain results (cluster-level FWE correction, voxel-wise p<0.001) with tables of coordinates. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength (Siemens 3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for task-evoked, voxelwise cue>control contrasts using visual stimuli and reports whole-brain statistical results.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cue videos (cocaine and food) and continuous craving ratings. It includes within-participant contrasts isolating cocaine video effects relative to food (hierarchical regression and direct cocaine>food comparisons) and reports group-level, voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain analyses with cluster correction and ROI-corrected connectivity analyses). Results (activation maps and coordinates) are described in the main text and supplementary material is referenced. Participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Provided 'full text' is only a website privacy/cookie notice; core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is not present, so the study cannot be assessed against the review criteria. Therefore I exclude due to incomplete full text. Exclusion IDs met: none (E3-E6 not assessable/ not confirmed). Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met (cannot be confirmed from provided content): I3 (uncertain whether fMRI cue-reactivity with visual cues was used), I4 (no information on within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (no group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected results reported in the provided content), I6 (no qualifying voxelwise results available in tables/figures/supplement), I7 (participant and MRI details not available). Full text incomplete: true.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual alcohol images in recently detoxified alcohol-dependent patients. It includes a within-participant contrast (alcohol > neutral) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results (one-sample t-test and multiple regression) with correction for multiple comparisons (AlphaSim-derived cluster extent corresponding to PFWE < 0.05). Results are presented in tables and figures (e.g., Table 2a, Table 3, Figures 1–3), and the manuscript provides participant demographics (age/sex), cue type (visual alcohol vs neutral images), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5/SPM8). All required inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (pleasant, unpleasant, neutral, cigarette-related) and assesses cue-reactivity in smokers planning to quit. The study includes within-subject contrasts (cigarette-related, pleasant, unpleasant vs neutral) analyzed with whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects GLMs (FDR q<.01) and reports voxelwise results in figures and tables with Talairach coordinates. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI acquisition parameters, preprocessing (BrainVoyager), and statistical software are reported. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures referenced).

Exclusion is due to mismatch with the meta-analysis scope: the study used PET imaging ([15O]H2O PET) and script-guided auditory mental imagery rather than functional MRI with a clear visual cue component. While the paper provides a within-participant cue>control contrast (cocaine imagery vs neutral) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (SPM voxelwise analyses with coordinate tables/figures), it does not meet the required modality or visual-cue inclusion criterion. Inclusion IDs met: I4 (within-participant drug cues>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported), I6 (results reported in figures/tables/coordinates), I7 (participant and methods details reported). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (Functional MRI study with a clear visual cue component). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related task fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues and neutral visual controls, with within-subject drug>neutral contrasts and group-level voxelwise analyses. Methods report preprocessing and SPM8 regression, subject-level contrasts and random-effects second-level voxelwise t-tests with AlphaSim correction (whole-brain voxelwise thresholding). Participant demographics and MRI field strength (3.0 T) are reported. The manuscript includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (visual cues), I4 (within-participant drug>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results, AlphaSim-corrected), I6 (results reported in main text/ROIs with peak coordinates referenced), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, field strength, preprocessing/statistics reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This is an fMRI study using visual drug-related and pleasant cues (CSD+, CSP+) and neutral control images, meeting the visual cue requirement. The authors report within-participant contrasts (CSD+ vs CS− and CSP+ vs CS−) as primary neural measures. The paper includes group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (referenced in Tables S1–S2 and Figures S3–S4) and ROI analyses; voxelwise results are reported in supplementary materials, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results. Key methodological details (participants, MRI field strength=4T, preprocessing/statistical software=S﻿PM8, cue types) are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cannabis cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (cannabis-related vs neutral images). It includes within-participant contrasts ([cannabis – neutral]) entered at the group level, and reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-level FWE correction (group-level task-evoked results). Participant demographics (age, gender), MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (fMRIPrep), and statistical software (SPM12) are reported. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria relevant to the meta-analysis objective (visual cue-reactivity, within-subject cue>control contrast, qualifying group-level voxelwise results, and availability of coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria apply.

This study used an fMRI monetary reward-anticipation task with visual cues (arrow indicators), providing a within-subject contrast of monetary reward > verbal feedback. The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with small-volume correction and coordinate peaks (e.g., nucleus accumbens, DLPFC), and includes methodological details (3T scanner, SPM8 preprocessing/analysis) and participant demographics. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for non-drug (natural) reward cue-reactivity with visual stimuli and reports qualifying voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of cue-induced cocaine craving using audiovisual (visual+auditory) stimuli and includes within-participant contrasts between cocaine-cue and neutral segments; however, the analyses are region-of-interest (ROI) based (percent signal change and fraction of pixels exceeding an arbitrary correlation threshold in preselected neuroanatomic regions) rather than group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results reported as whole-brain or small-volume-corrected maps. No qualifying voxelwise SPM-style results or small-volume-corrected voxelwise statistics are presented, so it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cue videos (e-cigarette vs electronic toothbrush) in experienced e-cigarette users. It includes within-participant contrasts of e-cigarette cues > neutral cues and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results from a random-effects GLM with voxelwise maps corrected via a Monte-Carlo cluster-level procedure; Talairach coordinates and cluster results are reported. The paper provides MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager QX), cue type, and participant information. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text is complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using alcohol (drug) visual cues as distractors and includes within-participant contrasts (alcohol vs. neutral/scramble) and interaction contrasts. Group-level voxelwise second-level analyses were performed and reported using a voxel-wise threshold (p<0.001) with cluster-extent correction corresponding to pFWE<0.05; results are described in the main text and supplementary materials. Key methodological details (3T field strength, SPM8 preprocessing/statistics, cue type, participant demographics) are reported. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol stimuli (alcohol pictures vs neutral IAPS), with a within-participant contrast modeled as alcohol > neutral. The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results (voxel-wise thresholds, cluster-extent thresholds, tables/figures and supplement references), and provides participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software. Thus it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol cues and reports within-participant contrasts (ALC>BEV). The paper includes a priori ROI analyses and, importantly, an exploratory whole-brain general linear model relating incentive salience to alcohol cue reactivity with cluster-forming Z>2.3 and corrected cluster significance p<0.05 — i.e., group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain). Participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are reported. The full text contains Introduction, Methods (participants, cue task, preprocessing, stats), Results, and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues and neutral images (I3). It reports within-participant contrasts of heroin-related > neutral cues and relevant one-sample and two-sample group-level voxelwise t-tests (I4). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported with whole-brain family-wise error correction (p≤0.05) and anatomical loci (I5,I6). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistics (SPM5) are reported (I7). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis of task-evoked visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues in participants on methadone maintenance. The study reports a within-participant contrast (heroin-related > neutral) with group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (t-maps, table of coordinates; p<.0001, cluster-level corrected at whole-brain analysis). Core methods and results are present (introduction, methods, results, discussion), and necessary metadata are reported (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing with SPM5). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI visual cue-reactivity and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual alcohol pictures and a within-participant contrast (alcohol > neutral). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported (whole-brain analyses with voxel-wise p<.001 and cluster-extent FWE correction via AlphaSim), with clusters/tables and figures described. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5/SPM8) are reported. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking (drug) cue-reactivity using visual smoking pictures (I3). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of smoking>neutral cues (I4) with group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (thresholded at z>2.3, cluster p<0.05 corrected) and lists activations/coordinates in the text and supplementary tables (satisfies I5 and I6). Methods include preprocessing and software (FSL) and participant sex/characteristics are reported; MRI field strength is not explicitly stated but missing details alone do not preclude inclusion (I7 is considered non-exclusionary). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical perfusion fMRI study of cigarette cue reactivity using audio-visual (visual) smoking cues, with a within-participant contrast of smoking cues > nonsmoking control cues. Group-level voxelwise SPM analyses are reported (both unmasked whole-brain cluster results and small-volume-corrected ROI results) with coordinates and statistical maps; craving–activation correlations are reported at corrected thresholds. Participant demographics, cue type, field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2) are described. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study using visual cues (shapes indicating effort and monetary reward) to probe neural responses to a natural reward (monetary) anticipation/valuation task. The study reports within-participant event-related regressors for cue presentation and combined-group validation analyses showing ventral striatum and dACC activations (i.e., cue-related > baseline effects). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results with FWE-corrected clusters and tables of coordinates for cue and feedback contrasts, satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise results. Participant demographics and MRI/preprocessing details are reported or referenced (Table 1 and Methods). Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking-related cues vs control images, reporting whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses (RFX ANOVA and RFX ANCOVA) with the within-participant contrast 'smoke > control' and corrected maps and coordinate tables. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/software (BrainVoyager) are reported. These elements satisfy the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for task-evoked visual cue-reactivity (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

The study used visual cue videos (gambling, cocaine, sad) and performed within-subject contrasts comparing cue conditions (e.g., cocaine vs other cues; gambling vs other cues), satisfying I3 and I4. Group-level voxelwise analyses of task-period intrinsic connectivity distribution (ICD) maps were reported, with a significant PCC cluster and MNI coordinates (voxelwise LME results reported at p<0.001 with cluster threshold), satisfying I5 and I6. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, BioImage Suite, AFNI) are reported, satisfying I7. The analysis is task-related whole-brain voxelwise (connectivity metric derived during task blocks), not an ROI-only, seed-only, or resting-state-only study; no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is included for the meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual-only stimuli (alcohol vs non-alcohol pictures) embedded in a visual oddball task. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol distractors > non-alcohol distractors (AD vs NAD) and related AD-NAD contrasts. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported: whole-brain voxelwise rmANOVA with FWE-corrected clusters (left IPL, right dorsal ACC) and a priori amygdala small-volume ROI analyses (age-adjusted z-scores) with significance testing. Methods report participant age/group, MRI field strength (Siemens Trio 3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, SPM5). These elements satisfy I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and is included.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (50 alcohol pictures vs 50 neutral pictures) with a within-subject contrast Alcohol>Neutral. Group-level voxelwise results are reported: Alcohol>Neutral contrast images entered into second-level random-effects analyses; significant activations survived small-volume FWE-correction within a priori striatal ROIs (ventral striatum and putamen), and whole-brain exploratory results are also presented. MRI field strength (3T Philips), preprocessing and stats software (SPM8) and participant characteristics are reported. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria (no ROI-only-only, no connectivity-only, contains within-participant cue>control contrast, is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study in heroin-dependent participants using audiovisual drug-related (visual component present) and matched neutral cues. The paper reports within-subject contrasts of heroin>neutral conditions and a group-level whole-brain voxelwise 2×2 ANOVA (cluster-corrected) with reported cluster locations/coordinates (tables/figures). Methods include MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and analysis software (FSL/FEAT), and participant age/sex information. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images of alcoholic vs non-alcoholic beverages) and reports within-subject ALC>BEV contrasts. The paper includes group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (cluster-corrected, Z>2.3, cluster P<0.05) with reported cluster coordinates (Table 3 and figures), satisfying the requirement for a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of active cocaine users using visual cocaine-related background pictures versus neutral backgrounds (visual cue component). The authors report within-participant contrasts comparing cocaine-related versus neutral backgrounds and interaction contrasts (high WM cocaine > high WM neutral). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported with voxelwise and cluster thresholds (t=4.14, p≤.001; cluster-size correction via Monte Carlo), and ROI analyses are additionally reported. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

Study is an empirical fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) visual cue reactivity using block-design visual food images (high-calorie, low-calorie, and objects). First-level within-participant contrasts (food > objects; high-calorie > low-calorie) are defined and group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM8. Results include small-volume-corrected voxelwise findings within a priori ROIs (hypothalamus, OFC, insula, DLPFC, nucleus accumbens) with FWE-corrected thresholds and reported coordinates/figures. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol-related images (alcoholic vs non-alcoholic beverage images) with a within-participant contrast (alcohol>non-alcohol) at the group level. The manuscript reports voxelwise task-evoked results (one-sample t-test, voxel-level analyses with MNI coordinates and cluster reporting) and provides figures/tables of activations. fMRI acquisition (3T), preprocessing and SPM8 are described. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity, within-subject cue>control contrasts, and group-level voxelwise statistical reporting. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (alcohol pictures) and a within-subject contrast of alcohol cues > neutral stimuli. Group-level voxelwise results are reported, including small-volume-corrected (SVC) ventral striatum findings (p<0.05 FWE for VOI) and MNI coordinates. Methods report participant age/sex (all male, ages provided), cue type, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts).

The provided full text is incomplete (only References and metadata). I cannot verify core methods/results needed to assess eligibility. Specifically, there is no information about the presence of a visual cue component, the within-participant cue>control contrasts, or reporting of group-level voxelwise (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) task-evoked results. Therefore I cannot confirm inclusion criteria. Exclusion is due to incomplete full text preventing assessment, not because any exclusion criterion is clearly met.

This is a task-evoked fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol cues (ALC vs BEV) in individuals with AUD. The manuscript reports a within-participant ALC>BEV contrast and describes a whole-brain group-level analysis of the ALC vs BEV contrast (see Supplementary Fig/Table) confirming mesocorticolimbic activation, satisfying the requirement for a group-level voxelwise result (whole-brain). Although the paper extracts ROI percent signal change from the bilateral ventral striatum, the presence of the whole-brain analyses in the supplement fulfills the meta-analysis’ requirement for voxelwise results. The methods report MRI field strength (3.0 T), preprocessing/software (FSL), participant demographics, and cue type. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual drug-related word cues and matched neutral words, with within-participant contrasts (drug > neutral) reported. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-level correction and a small-volume correction for the mesencephalon are reported with stereotaxic coordinates and cluster statistics. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (4T), preprocessing, and SPM2 software are described. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; missing supplemental materials are acceptable. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual cannabis vs. neutral images (Cannabis Cue Reactivity task). It reports within-participant cannabis>neutral contrasts and second-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (cluster thresholded, z>2.58, FWE-corrected p<0.05) with reported significant clusters (pMCC) and peak coordinates. MRI field strength (Siemens 3.0T PrismaFit) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are described. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for voxelwise task-evoked visual cue-reactivity results and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is a study protocol/RCT planning fMRI cue-reactivity and rtfMRI neurofeedback using visual alcohol cues, but it does not report any original task-evoked voxelwise fMRI results. Inclusion met: I3 (fMRI study with visual alcohol cues). Inclusion not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast results are presented) and I5 (no group-level whole-brain or SVC voxelwise task-evoked results reported). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (non-empirical/paper without original human fMRI data reported). Full text appears complete as a protocol, but contains no empirical results, so study must be excluded from a meta-analysis requiring task-evoked voxelwise results.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual heroin-related and pleasant (IAPS) cues in abstinent opioid-dependent males and healthy controls. It reports within-subject contrasts (heroin vs. baseline/neutral; pleasant vs. baseline) and group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses with coordinates and statistical thresholds (FDR-corrected; voxelwise results reported via coordinates). Relevant participant details (age, sex), cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (500-ms images) with within-subject contrasts (cocaine > neutral) and group-level voxelwise analyses. The paper reports ROI-based and whole-brain cluster-corrected voxelwise results (tables/figures) and provides necessary methodological details (participant demographics, cue types, 3T scanner, preprocessing with SPM8, statistical software). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-evoked fMRI study of visual natural reward (food) cue reactivity using a standardized food image viewing task. It reports within-participant contrasts (food > non-food and high-calorie > low-calorie) at the group level, with voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM12) and cluster-thresholded results and coordinates (supplementary materials and NeuroVault maps). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3.0T Philips), preprocessing and statistical software are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

The study is an fMRI cue-reactivity experiment using visual alcohol images (meets I3). It reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses conducted in SPM12 with FWE thresholds (meets I5) and provides coordinate/analysis detail (meets I6) and participant/MRI/preprocessing details (meets I7). However, the authors explicitly modelled ‘alcohol’ and ‘neutral’ conditions separately and state they did not combine these into an ‘alcohol versus neutral’ within-participant difference contrast; no within-participant alcohol>neutral voxelwise contrast is reported. Thus the required within-participant cue>control contrast is not present (I4 not met). Per the review exclusion rules, this study is excluded because it reports task-evoked results without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast (exclusion criterion E5).

This study is an fMRI investigation of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual alcohol-related vs. neutral pictures (visual cues). It reports within-participant contrast images (alcohol > neutral) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM, AlphaSim cluster correction to pFWE < 0.05). Participant demographics and MRI acquisition/preprocessing/statistical details are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (visual cue component, within-participant cue>control contrast, and qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes task-evoked voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (120 food pictures) and scrambled control images, employing within-subject contrasts (food > control) across nicotine/placebo sessions. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported (whole-brain analyses with PFWE values and coordinate tables; small-volume/ROI analyses also reported), with preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5), MRI field strength (3T), and participant demographics (age, sex, BMI) provided. Therefore it meets all meta-analysis inclusion requirements for visual cue-based natural reward fMRI studies. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes task-evoked voxelwise results; includes within-participant cue>control contrasts; is empirical). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity used visual alcohol images and neutral beverage controls (I3). It reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol>neutral beverage (I4) and presents group-level voxelwise analyses (second-level random effects, cluster-corrected within the striatum, with reported MNI coordinates and corrected p-values), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results (I5, I6). The paper reports participant sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5), addressing reporting preferences (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not limited to ROI-only results (E3), are task-evoked rather than connectivity/resting-state only (E4), include the required within-participant cue>control contrasts (not only between-group contrasts; E5), and are empirical human fMRI data (not a review; E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study used visual food cues (high- vs low-calorie images), tested a within-participant contrast (high-calorie > low-calorie), and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results using an anatomical ROI with FWE small-volume correction and peak coordinates (MNI). Methods report participants’ age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software. These satisfy the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for natural reward visual cue-reactivity and the qualifying voxelwise small-volume-corrected result.

This fMRI study uses visual smoking cues (images of hands holding cigarettes vs neutral objects) and includes a within-participant contrast (smoking cue > neutral cue). Task-evoked voxelwise statistical results are reported: ROI-based small-volume-corrected (SVC) analyses on PCC/SCC with peak-level FWE-P < .05 (PCC) and exploratory whole-brain cluster-level FWE results. Methods report MRI field strength (3.0T), software (SPM12, CONN), and participant age/sex information. Thus it meets the review objective and satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this is an fMRI study using visual cues (Monetary Incentive Delay) assessing natural reward-related cue reactivity, the manuscript reports only ROI-based analyses (beta extraction from a priori small spherical ROIs) and mediation analyses on those ROI betas. There are no group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results reported (neither whole-brain nor small-volume-corrected voxelwise results or coordinate tables). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI with visual reward cues) and I7 (reporting demographics and methods details) are satisfied; key inclusion criterion I5 (at least one qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked result whole-brain or SVC) is not met, and a within-participant cue>control voxelwise contrast (I4) is not clearly reported. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical human fMRI study using clear visual drug cues (images of cocaine powder vs neutral images) embedded in a task. The paper reports within-participant contrasts comparing cocaine-related versus neutral cue conditions (cocaine vs neutral during inhibitory-control trials) and presents group-level voxelwise second-level whole-brain analyses (GLM-Flex) thresholded voxelwise and cluster-level FWE-corrected, as well as ROI analyses (STN). Participant demographics and MRI details are reported. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study that includes clear visual stimuli (unimodal pictures and bimodal picture+odor trials). The manuscript reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., cannabis picture > flower picture; cannabis picture > baseline) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected z≥2.3, p<.05) as well as small-volume ROI analyses. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, AFNI, ANTS) are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not include a visual cue component (inclusion criterion I3 not met). The paradigm used individualized auditory guided imagery scripts (audio presentation and mental imagery), not visual-only or multimodal designs that include visual cues. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant contrasts between favorite-food, stress, and neutral-relaxing conditions were performed), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results reported via whole-brain ICD analyses with FWE correction), I6 (voxelwise results reported in text/figures), and I7 (participant and methods details reported). Exclusion criteria met: none. Because I3 is required for the meta-analysis objective (visual cue-reactivity), the study must be excluded despite meeting other criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of smokers using visual cues (personal and standard smoking vs nonsmoking environments and proximal cues). It includes within-subject contrasts of smoking>nonsmoking stimuli (e.g., PSEs vs PNEs and smoking vs nonsmoking proximal cues) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (cluster-corrected threshold z=3.1, p<0.05) identifying activation clusters (insula, striatum, parietal cortex, etc.). Results (including supplementary tables/figures) provide voxelwise task-evoked statistical findings. Methods report participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL). Core article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of tobacco cue-reactivity using visual smoking and neutral images, with within-participant contrasts (smoking-related cues > neutral cues) reported. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain results are presented (cluster-thresholded Z>2.3, p<.05) with coordinates/tables and figures. Methods report MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL). Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking cue-reactivity using visual smoking-related pictures with within-subject contrasts (smoking vs. neutral). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise 2×2 ANOVA and follow-up t-tests are reported with FWE-corrected results and coordinate tables/figures. Methods report participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), cue type, preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI), and task design. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and reports methodological details satisfying I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study uses visual cue-reactivity (video-based heroin and neutral cues), includes within-participant contrasts (heroin-cue vs neutral within runs; A2 vs A1) and reports group-level voxelwise results (cluster-thresholded, Talairach coordinates, Table I; Monte Carlo/Alphasim correction). Methods report MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing (AFNI), participant demographics, and cue details. Voxelwise task-evoked statistical results are presented in text, tables, and figures, satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol cues in individuals with AUD. The manuscript reports within-subject alcohol>control cue contrasts (sample-level alcohol vs control activation clusters) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain results (cluster-corrected, MNI coordinates provided) including treatment-related BOLD differences. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (fMRIPrep) and SPM12 statistical analysis are described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for visual cue-reactivity, within-participant cue>control contrasts, and whole-brain voxelwise reporting. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking cue-reactivity using visual image stimuli. The authors report a within-participant contrast (smoking > neutral images) and performed group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects ANCOVA) with whole-brain cluster correction; results are reported as cluster coordinates (Table 1) and figures. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (photographs), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager QX) are provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly assesses addiction-related cue-reactivity using visual cues (alcohol and gambling images) presented during task fMRI. The authors report a within-subject contrast comparing addiction-related versus neutral cues ([BA + SA] > [BN + SN]) and present voxelwise, whole-brain task-evoked results (cluster-defining p=0.001, whole-brain FWE p<0.05) for cue-reactivity and other contrasts; whole-brain maps are available (NeuroVault). Key methodological details required by I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software SPM12) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control, empirical fMRI data present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3–I7 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study using pictorial alcohol cues (visual stimuli) in adolescents with AUD. The experiment includes within-subject contrasts of alcoholic > nonalcohol pictures and reports group-level voxelwise statistical comparisons (independent-samples t tests, clusterwise correction with voxelwise and clusterwise P thresholds) with coordinates/tables/figures. AFNI preprocessing/statistics are described. Although MRI field strength is not explicitly stated, this is a preferred (not mandatory) item and does not preclude inclusion. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This study is an fMRI investigation of effort-based decision-making using monetary reward and effort cues, not a drug- or natural reward-cue reactivity paradigm. Although it reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (I5) and provides voxelwise results/tables (I6) and reports participant demographics, cue type (monetary/effort), MRI field strength, and preprocessing/software details (I7), it does not present a within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli or natural reward-related cues > control stimuli (I4 not met). It also does not implement a visual drug-cue reactivity design (I3 not met). Therefore exclusion criterion E5 applies (no qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast), so the study cannot be included in this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking (drug) cue-reactivity using visual pictorial stimuli. It reports within-subject contrasts of smoking-related > neutral cues at the group level and provides voxelwise task-evoked results with stereotactic coordinates and statistical thresholds (e.g., smoking vs. neutral, p<0.001 uncorrected; regression results reported with coordinates at p<0.005 uncorrected). Methods report MRI field strength (3.0 T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5), participant age/sex, and cue type. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and none of the exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

Excluded per E3: This fMRI study used visual smoking cues (I3) and reported within-participant smoking>neutral contrasts (I4), and provided participant demographics (I7). However, reported analyses rely on ROI-extracted beta weights (caudate/NAc) and regression on those ROI values; the paper does not report any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical results required by I5. Therefore it fails I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study in patients with alcohol use disorder using visual picture stimuli. The within-subject design included a picture-type factor (alcohol vs control) constituting a within-participant cue>control contrast (though no significant picture-type effects were observed). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results are reported (voxelwise ANOVA clusters with MNI coordinates shown in main/supplementary tables), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain/small-volume-corrected reporting. Participant groups (AUD patients and healthy controls) and task design are appropriate for inclusion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods summary, results and supplementary tables with voxelwise coordinates, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol images and IAPS affective pictures). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol > neutral) and pre-to-post (post>pre) within-psilocybin effects, and treatment-by-time group-level voxelwise analyses. Whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (cluster tables/figures; p-uncorrected <0.005) and seed-based gPPI connectivity is secondary. MRI acquisition parameters and preprocessing/statistical software (Siemens Skyra, SPM12, CONN) and participant demographics are reported. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Thus the study meets the review’s criteria for visual cue-based drug cue reactivity with qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked results and is appropriate for inclusion.

Although this is an fMRI cue‐reactivity study of cannabis that includes clear visual cues (and reports participant demographics), the paper reports ROI/network-based dynamic functional connectivity (DCC) analyses and topological metrics rather than any group-level voxelwise task-evoked activation contrasts or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results. The meta-analysis requires at least one qualifying within-participant voxelwise cue>control contrast (whole-brain or SVC). Because the study provides only connectivity/ROI analyses (no qualifying voxelwise task activation results), it meets exclusion criteria E3 and E4. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual cues present), I7 (demographic and methodological details reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant voxelwise cue>control contrast reported), I5/I6 (no qualifying whole-brain or SVC voxelwise results available). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (Alcohol Pictures Task) with college students. It reports within-participant alcohol vs. non-alcohol beverage contrasts and group-level voxelwise whole-brain ANOVA results with cluster-wise whole-brain correction (clusters >2619 µl, voxel-wise F(2,40)>3.23, p<.05, whole-brain corrected p<.05) and cluster coordinates in Table 3. Methods report MRI field strength (Siemens 3T), preprocessing (SPM5) and group analysis in AFNI. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for voxelwise task-evoked cue>control results and contains sufficient methodological detail. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, lacking within-participant cue>control contrast, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual drug and food images (visual cues). It contains within-participant contrasts (e.g., look drug>look neutral; look drug>look food; savor food>look food; reappraise drug>look drug) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results with cluster-defining thresholds and peak coordinates (see Table 2 and figures). Participant demographics, MRI acquisition, preprocessing, and analysis software are reported. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is available. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria for visual cue component, within-participant cue>control contrasts, and qualifying whole-brain voxelwise group-level task-evoked results.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cigarette cue reactivity using visual stimuli (2-min smoking videos vs matched neutral videos). It uses within-subject contrasts of smoking>neutral, reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain cluster-corrected statistical results with peak coordinates and tables, and presents task-evoked results in figures/tables. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided full text. Therefore it fulfills the meta-analysis requirements for visual cue component, within-participant cue>control contrast, and qualifying voxelwise task-evoked group results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

The full text is an empirical fMRI study presenting visual cannabis, sexual, aversive, and neutral cues using a backward-masking paradigm. It reports within-subject voxelwise group-level contrasts (cannabis > neutral, sexual > neutral, aversive > neutral) with coordinates and cluster-corrected significance within an a priori ROI mask (small-volume correction) and provides methodological details (3T scanner, SPM8 preprocessing, participant demographics). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue fMRI), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise results with small-volume-correction), I6 (results reported as coordinates/tables), and I7 (participant/cue/MRI/preprocessing details). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This empirical fMRI study explicitly examines alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol, stress, neutral images) and includes within-participant contrasts (alcohol cues > neutral and stress > neutral). Analyses are whole-brain voxelwise with family-wise error correction (p<0.001, cluster p<0.05) and report peak MNI coordinates and cluster results in main text/figures (supplement referenced). MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (BioImageSuite), and statistical methods (AFNI 3dClustSim) are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and violates no exclusion criteria.

The article reports an empirical fMRI study using visual stimuli (smoking and food videos) making it relevant to drug and natural reward visual cue-reactivity. It includes within-participant contrasts (Smoking>Food, Smoking>Baseline, Food>Baseline). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported with cluster-corrected thresholds and coordinate tables (Table 1, Tables 2–3), satisfying whole-brain/statistically corrected reporting. Results are available in text, figures, and tables. Participant demographics and MRI/preprocessing details are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is excluded because it does not include a clear visual cue component (it uses individualized script-driven imagery for stress, drug/alcohol cue, and neutral-relaxing conditions), thus failing inclusion criterion I3. Satisfied inclusion criteria: I4 (within-participant contrasts: drug-cue vs neutral condition reported), I5 (whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results with family-wise error correction), I6 (results reported in figures/tables/supplement), and I7 (participant demographics and methodological details reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study using visual alcohol-associated cues with healthy controls and abstinent alcoholics. It reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol-related > control stimuli (visual neutral and scrambled) and presents group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with small-volume correction (threshold P<0.05 corrected) in predefined ROIs including striatum, ACC and mPFC; coordinates and tables/figures of activation are provided. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type (visual), MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. Therefore the study meets the inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (full-color cocaine and neutral images). The design includes within-participant contrasts (cocaine blocks > neutral cocaine blocks; negative emotional > neutral emotional) entered into group-level analyses. The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results (FWE cluster-level corrected; tables provided for cocaine and emotional cue contrasts), and includes required methodological details (participant age/sex, cue types, 3.0T scanner, preprocessing with fMRIPrep, SPM12). Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study that includes visual cue elements (images of cues presented and tactile+visual cue exposures) and tests within-participant contrasts (MJ cue > fruit cue) used as the primary imaging contrast. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported via whole-brain voxelwise PLSC analyses with cluster/voxel tables (supplemental tables) and cluster coordinates; MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT, R PLSC), participant ages, and cue types are reported. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not only connectivity/resting-state, and include the required within-participant cue>control contrast. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (picture-perception task) with a within-subject contrast of alcohol cues > control stimuli. Group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (whole-brain one-sample t-test, FWE-corrected) and small-volume-corrected ROI analyses in the ventral striatum (FWE-corrected). Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state, includes within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports a cue-elicited craving task but does not present any within-participant voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., drug-cues > control) or group-level voxelwise/small-volume-corrected activation results. Analyses are ROI-based functional connectivity and graph-classification (AWFC, degree centrality, network community), with no task-evoked voxelwise statistical maps or coordinate tables qualifying for inclusion. Therefore it meets exclusion criteria E3 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying voxelwise result), E4 (reports connectivity/graph-based analyses without task-evoked voxelwise results), and E5 (focuses on between-group classification/community differences without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criterion I7 (reporting of participant age/sex, MRI field strength, preprocessing) is satisfied, but I3 (clear visual cue component), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked result), and I6 (availability of qualifying voxelwise results in figures/tables) are not met. Full text appears complete (contains methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of smoking cue-reactivity that includes visual cues both alone (unisensory) and combined with odor (multisensory), directly addressing the review objective. The study reports within-participant contrasts of drug cues > neutral (CIG-I > NEU-I) under odorless and cigarette-odor conditions. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster-corrected, Z>2.3, p<0.05), satisfying the requirement for qualifying voxelwise results. Results are presented in the main text and figures/tables; participant demographics (age/sex), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT) are all reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not assess drug- or natural reward–related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and does not include any within-participant cue>control contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked fMRI results from an N-back working memory task) and I7 (reports participant age/sex and MRI details). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no assessment of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with visual cues) and I4 (no within-participant drug-cue>control or natural-reward-cue>control contrast). Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E6 apply exactly (the study is not only ROI-only, it includes voxelwise task results; it is not only resting-state/ connectivity-only; and it does not present only between-group contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore it does not satisfy the primary scope of the meta-analysis and should be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual alcohol-related pictures (I3). The main within-participant contrast alcohol > neutral is reported and used in group analyses (I4). Group-level voxelwise results are reported using whole-brain analyses and small-volume FWE-corrected results in striatal regions (I5), with coordinate reporting and figures/tables referenced (I6). Participant demographics, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing (SPM5), and statistical software are described (I7). No exclusion criteria are met: the study does not rely solely on ROI-only analyses (E3), connectivity-only or resting-state analyses (E4), nor does it only report between-group contrasts without within-participant cue>control contrasts (E5). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete for screening. Therefore, the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue reactivity using visual pictorial stimuli and within-subject contrasts. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol > soft drink) and pre/post training contrasts, and presents group-level voxelwise results with small-volume correction (family-wise error corrected) in anatomically defined ROIs (amygdala, nucleus accumbens) with peak coordinates and statistics. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplemental materials are not required for eligibility. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical human fMRI study of smoking cue reactivity using audiovisual (multimodal including visual) cues.
