No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper is not eligible for a meta-analysis restricted to studies that include a visual cue component in the fMRI task.

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation of alcohol cue-reactivity using clearly presented visual cues (alcohol, food, neutral symbols) and reports within-subject contrasts of alcohol cues versus control stimuli (high-threat alcohol cues contrasted with high-threat food and neutral cues). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported (whole-brain analyses with cluster correction via AFNI 3dClustSim) and ROI analyses/small-volume approaches are also described. Voxelwise results are described in the main text and linked to figures/supplement. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, CONN) are reported. Full article content (background, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the manuscript meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study uses visual heroin-related cues and reports within-participant contrasts (heroin-related > neutral) at the group level, but the reported voxelwise results are confined to a priori ROI masks and thresholded uncorrected (p<0.05, cluster>20 voxels) rather than reported as whole-brain corrected or small-volume-corrected results. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results with no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise result) and does not meet inclusion criterion I5. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I6 (voxelwise results reported in figures/main text), I7 (reporting of age/sex, cue type, field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise result). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of drug (cocaine) cue-reactivity in regular users with a described cue-reactivity task during fMRI, within-subject analyses of cue responses, and reported exploratory whole-brain analyses (with comprehensive results referenced in supplementary materials). The full text includes introduction, methods (participants, MRI acquisition at 3.0T, tasks), results, and discussion. Although the cue modality is not explicitly spelled out in the main text, cue-reactivity paradigms typically use visual cues and the manuscript states the cue-reactivity task was adopted from prior work; voxelwise whole-brain results are reported/exploratory and available in supplements (satisfying whole-brain/SVC reporting criteria). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete.

Exclusion (E3) applies: the manuscript reports only ROI-based analyses (predefined 6-mm spherical ROIs with extracted BOLD timecourses entered into HLM/GLM) and does not present any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical maps. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual image cues), I4 (within-participant contrast ALC>BEV was computed), I7 (participant age range, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, HLM, SPSS) are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no qualifying whole-brain or SVC voxelwise group-level results reported). Full text appears complete (contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded per E3.

Full text (abstract and metadata) indicates an fMRI cue-reactivity study using alcohol-related vs neutral video sequences in abstinent alcoholics (visual cues) and reports a within-subject alcohol vs neutral contrast. However, the primary reported significant findings are from psychophysiological interaction (PPI) seed-based connectivity analyses (regions more connected with posterior cingulate cortex during alcohol cues). The simple task contrast alcohol>neutral was reported as not significant. There is no evidence in the available content of a group-level voxelwise task-evoked activation result (whole-brain or SVC) qualifying for inclusion. The provided content appears to be incomplete (abstract/metadata/references only), preventing verification of any unreported voxelwise results in the full paper or supplements. Therefore the study is excluded under E4.

The full text contains a visual smoking-cue paradigm (videos) and reports within-participant contrasts (smoking cue vs fixation baseline; alcohol cue vs baseline). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses are described (voxel-wise one-sample t tests across subjects with FDR control and cluster-wise inference; whole-brain activation maps and clusters are reported and plotted). Methods report participant demographics, scanner (3T), and preprocessing (FSL). Although the alcohol cue was a taste stimulus, the study is multimodal and includes clear visual cue components, satisfying the meta-analysis focus on visual cue-reactivity. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete for screening.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images. It includes within-participant contrasts (HC vs LC food cues) and reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain results (second-level repeated-measures ANOVA) with cluster-level FWE correction. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12), participant demographics (age/sex), and cue types. Results (DLPFC activation, PPI connectivity) are reported in the main text with references to supplementary tables/figures. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains qualifying within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is an empirical human fMRI study).

This fMRI study investigates Pavlovian-to-instrumental transfer using monetary Pavlovian cues and reports whole-brain voxelwise results for incongruent vs congruent (monetary) contrasts. Although alcohol/water images were presented in a subset of trials, the authors explicitly disregarded these alcohol/water-background trials in the main analyses, and no within-participant drug-cue > control-stimulus voxelwise group-level contrast for alcohol cues is reported in the primary results (any alcohol-related analyses are described as exploratory in Supporting Information). Therefore the study does not meet the key inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis: it does not assess drug/natural reward cue-reactivity with a qualifying within-participant drug-cue>control contrast (I3, I4) nor report a group-level voxelwise drug-cue reactivity result (I5). It does meet acceptability of reporting formats (I6) and reports participant/sample and MRI details (I7).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images. It includes within-participant contrasts comparing craved vs. control stimuli (Look Craved > Look Not Craved; Look Craved > Look Neutral) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results with cluster correction (AlphaSim) and coordinate tables. The paper also reports MRI field strength (3.0 T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), participant age/sex, and cue types. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, empirical data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (infant faces) probing a natural (social/caregiving) reward (baby schema). Within-subject contrasts were tested (baby faces vs fixation and High vs Low baby schema), and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (z-thresholding and cluster FWE correction) with cluster peaks in ventral striatum. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical BOLD fMRI study of smoking cue reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-subject cue>neutral contrasts (smoking cue minus neutral) and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (condition by NMR group ANOVA) with appropriate multiple-comparison correction, and reports cluster results and extracted percent signal changes. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, FILM) are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli (methamphetamine, sexual, neutral images) with within-participant contrasts (methamphetamine>neutral; sexual>neutral) reported. The paper includes group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (cluster-level FWE-corrected results with peak coordinates and cluster size reported for the left superior frontal cortex) and ROI analyses; voxelwise results are reported in the main text with coordinates. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue types, MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are described. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is excluded because the alcohol-cue manipulation used individualized guided imagery (audio/script-based) rather than a visual cue component required by the meta-analysis (I3 not met). The paper does include a within-participant alcohol-cue > neutral contrast (I4 met) and reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results with FWE correction (I5 met). Reporting of voxelwise results in figures/tables is present (I6 met), and participant/cue/MRI details are reported (I7 met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded due to failure to meet I3 (visual cue requirement).

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-subject contrasts including alcohol-cue viewing versus baseline (reported as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results with cluster-level FWE correction and coordinates/tables) and condition contrasts (prayer > passive/news) that modulate cue responses. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, NeuroElf), and participant characteristics are described. Results include whole-brain corrected voxelwise findings (tables/figures) meeting eligibility. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study that uses clear visual cues (abstract shapes predicting beer vs water), includes within-participant contrasts (beer>water) for anticipation/outcome/delivery, and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results (one-sample t-tests, one-way ANOVAs, regression) with coordinate foci and multiple-comparison correction. Results and thresholds are reported in the text and supplemented via NeuroVault. Participant characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, ICA-AROMA) are described. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual images of methamphetamine (drug) and sexual (natural reward) cues. The design includes within-subject contrasts (paired t-tests within groups assessing condition effects: sexual vs neutral and sexual vs MA cues) and a group-level voxelwise 2x3 within-subjects ANOVA reported with whole-brain cluster-level FWE correction, providing task-evoked voxelwise results (group-by-condition interaction). MRI field strength, preprocessing and analysis software are reported and participant demographics provided. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis objective and inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity, within-participant cue>control contrasts, and whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion E4 applies: the study reports only connectivity- and dynamics-based task analyses (miFC, brain state dynamics, PLS, eigenvector centrality from parcel-based analyses) and does not present any group-level voxelwise task-evoked activation results (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) or coordinate tables/figures of task activation contrasts. Inclusion I3 is met (fMRI cue-reactivity task with drug-related vs neutral visual cue blocks). Inclusion I4 is met in the sense that within-participant contrasts of drug cues > neutral cues were computed for connectivity metrics. Inclusion I5 is NOT met: no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise task-evoked statistical results are reported, so the key voxelwise activation requirement for the meta-analysis is absent. Therefore the paper must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This article is a narrative synthesis/review of a series of neuroimaging (ERP and fMRI) studies rather than a single empirical fMRI paper reporting new group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. The full text does not present original within-participant fMRI cue>control voxelwise contrasts (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) with coordinates or statistical maps required for inclusion. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical/review) and does not satisfy inclusion criteria I3, I4, or I5.

This study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation of alcohol cue reactivity using visual alcohol and non-alcohol beverage images, with a clear within-participant contrast (ALC vs BEV). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted (FSL FEAT/FLAME1) and reported with cluster-corrected maps and coordinates (Table 2, Fig. 1), satisfying requirements for voxelwise task-evoked results. Key methodological details (participant age/sex, cue type, 3.0 T MRI, preprocessing and software—FSL v6.0.1) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the meta-analysis requirement for a visual cue component (I3). The cue-reactivity task used gustatory (taste) alcohol cues delivered via a gustometer (alcohol vs lychee juice) and did not present alcohol-related visual stimuli or a multimodal design that clearly includes visual cues. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant contrast alcohol>control present), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked whole-brain results reported and corrected), I6 (voxelwise results reported in main text/figures/supplement), and I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength [3T], and preprocessing/statistical software). Exclusion criteria: none applicable (E3–E6 not met). Full text appears complete and provides methods, results, and discussion. Therefore excluded based on failure to satisfy I3 (no visual cue).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (70 food images vs 70 non-food images) and a within-subjects placebo/insulin design. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (food > non-food) and task-evoked, group-level voxelwise results with family-wise-error correction and small-volume ROI correction (NAc, VTA) and provides peak coordinates. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (SPM12, GLM denoise) and analysis software are reported. Results include whole-brain and small-volume-corrected voxelwise findings and coordinates, satisfying the meta-analysis inclusion requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, empirical human fMRI data). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Exclusion E3 met: the study reports ROI-based analyses and used ROI-extracted contrast values in regressions, but did not report any qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) significant activation for the cocaine>neutral contrast. Inclusion met: I3 (visual cue component — cocaine words presented visually) and I4 (within-participant contrast cocaine>neutral was computed). Inclusion not met: I5 (no qualifying group-level voxelwise result reported as significant/usable for meta-analysis), I6 (no available qualifying voxelwise coordinates/peaks to include), I7 (reporting details partially present but not sufficient to rescue lack of qualifying voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking-related vs neutral images). It includes within-subject contrasts (smoking-related > neutral) at the group level, using whole-brain random-effects voxelwise GLM with cluster-size correction; results are reported with corrected thresholds and coordinate tables/figures. Participant details (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager QX) are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that used visual stimuli (visual and auditory cues; visual component present). Within-subject contrasts comparing high- vs. low-calorie food cues (cue>control type contrast) are reported pre- and post-surgery. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted using SPM5 with cluster-extent correction (p<0.05 corrected) and results are reported in text/figures; details on participants (age, sex), cue types, scanner field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) with within-participant contrasts (WATCH Food > WATCH Neutral) reported as voxelwise group-level results (activation maps, thresholding, and MNI coordinates). Methods report scanner field strength (3T), SPM8 preprocessing/statistics, participant age/sex, and cue type. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical human fMRI study using visual smoking cues (and matched control images) in a within-subject, placebo-controlled design. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (smoking>control) and presents group-level voxelwise analyses (whole-brain repeated-measures ANOVA) with FDR-corrected results in ventral striatum and additional voxelwise results (p<0.001 uncorrected) reported in tables/figures. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistics software (SPM2). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue conditioning using novel visual stimuli (geometric CS) with within-subject contrasts between CS+ (alcohol-paired) and CS− (saline-paired). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses were performed (SPM5), with whole-brain cluster-corrected results reported and coordinates provided. Participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity- or resting-state-only; includes within-participant cue contrasts; is original empirical fMRI data). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual anticipatory cues (shapes) signaling monetary rewards/losses (natural reward). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of reward-cue > non-incentive cue (anticipation) and outcome contrasts, and group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster-based correction (voxelwise ANOVA, reported suprathreshold clusters). Methods report participant age/sex, cue types, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistics (AFNI). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I6 (results clearly available in main text/tables/figures), and I7 (reported participant and imaging details). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol pictures). The task used visual-only alcohol vs neutral blocks and computed within-subject contrast 'alcohol—neutral' per participant. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (cluster thresholds, tables and figures reporting peak coordinates and significant clusters). Participant demographics (N=86, sex), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5/SPM8) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrast, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7).

The study is an original task-based fMRI study with within-subject cue>control contrasts (gain cue > neutral cue, loss cue > neutral cue) and reports group-level voxelwise results with small-volume correction. However, it does not examine drug-related cues (e.g., alcohol images) or natural reward-related cues (e.g., erotic or other primary reward images). Instead, it uses a monetary incentive delay (MID) task with monetary cues (secondary reinforcers). Therefore inclusion criterion I3 (drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with a visual cue component) is not met. Met inclusion criteria: I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts present), I5 (group-level voxelwise results with SVC reported), I6 (results available in main/supplementary materials), I7 (participant sex, cue type, and preprocessing/statistical software reported; MRI field strength likely in appendix but missing would not alone exclude). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a behavioral cue-reactivity study using personalized videotaped and in vivo alcohol cues; it does not report any functional MRI data or MRI methods, and no voxelwise task-evoked group-level results are presented. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none of the listed exclusion criteria (E3–E6) explicitly apply. (b) Inclusion IDs met: none — although the study uses visual cues, it is not an fMRI study. (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (not a functional MRI study), I4 (no within-participant fMRI cue>control contrast reported), I5 (no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results), I6 (no qualifying voxelwise results reported), and I7 (MRI details not reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) but contains no fMRI analyses. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to meet core fMRI-specific inclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study using a monetary incentive delay (MID) task with clearly defined visual cues (geometric figures) predicting monetary gain/loss/neutral outcomes, meeting the review’s focus on visual natural-reward cue reactivity. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (gain > neutral; loss > neutral) at the group level and provides voxelwise statistical results (including coordinates) and small-volume-corrected (SVC, FWE-corrected) findings in the ventral striatum. Methods report participant demographics (male, age-matched groups), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5), satisfying reporting preferences. The supplied full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: the cue paradigm is individualized audio-guided script-driven imagery (auditory/imaginal cues) rather than visual or multimodal designs that include a visual cue component required by the meta-analysis. The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I4 (within-participant contrasts of drug/stress vs neutral), I5 (whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results with FWE correction), I6 (reporting of voxel coordinates/figures), and I7 (reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Exclusion is based solely on failure to satisfy I3 (lack of visual cue component).

This study reports task-evoked visual cue-reactivity using alcohol (visual) stimuli and alternative goal images (I3). It includes within-participant contrasts (alcohol > neutral) via a group random-effects GLM (I4) and reports whole-brain voxelwise results with cluster correction (Monte-Carlo; I5). Results are presented in figures/tables and supplementary material (I6). Participant age/sex, cue type, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported; MRI field strength is not explicitly stated (I7 is preferred but not required). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so is complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (favorite alcoholic drink images vs water) during a Pavlovian-instrumental transfer task. It includes within-subject contrasts comparing alcohol-related versus control (water/neutral) stimuli and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with a small-volume-corrected (SVC) finding in the right ventral striatum (NAcc; pFWE−SVC = 0.01). The paper provides participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (Siemens Trio 3 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate any exclusion criteria. The full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cue images and reports within-subject cue>control contrasts (Alcohol cue > Neutral). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain LME analyses are reported with family-wise error correction (FWE) and cluster correction, and results are presented in figures/tables (Supplemental Table ST1), satisfying the requirement for qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results. The manuscript provides participant demographics (age range and sex counts), cue type (visual alcohol cues), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (BioImageSuite, AFNI), meeting reporting preferences. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is original human fMRI data). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual drug cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

Only a brief summary/abstract is provided; the full article (methods, detailed results, voxelwise statistics/coordinates) is not available here, so fulltext is incomplete. Inclusion criterion I3 is met (an fMRI study using alcohol-related visual stimuli). However, I cannot verify I4 (presence of a within-participant cue>control contrast) because the summary describes group activation in alcoholics versus controls but does not state that a within-subject cue>control contrast was performed or reported. I cannot verify I5 (reporting of group-level voxelwise whole-brain or SVC results) or I6 (availability of voxelwise results/coordinates in tables/figures) from the provided content. No exclusion criteria are explicitly met based on the summary. Exclusion is due to incomplete full text preventing confirmation of required voxelwise within-participant analyses and reporting.

This fMRI study used a monetary incentive delay task with visual cues indicating monetary gains/losses vs neutral cues, providing within-participant contrasts (gain>neutral and loss>neutral). The manuscript reports voxelwise task-evoked results: one-sample and group-level whole-brain FWE-corrected activations (e.g., VS) and ROI analyses using small-volume correction. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12/MATLAB) are reported. The full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of natural reward-related (monetary) cue-reactivity with visual cues and reports qualifying voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual alcohol-related pictures versus neutral IAPS pictures (visual cues). It includes a within-participant contrast CUEalc > IAPSneutral and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results analyzed with SPM/BPM. Results are reported with small-volume FWE corrections in a priori ROIs and with whole-brain FWE-corrected peaks and coordinate tables/figures (Figures and Tables with MNI coordinates and FWE p-values). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8, BPM, ArtRepair) are reported. The full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (drug) cue-reactivity using visual smoking images. The report includes within-participant smoking>neutral contrasts and group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (cluster-corrected Z=2.3, p<0.05) with tables/coordinates. Participant demographics, MRI parameters, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity includes a clear visual cue component (visual labels presented during taste delivery), uses a within-participant Alcohol>Water contrast, and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (cluster-corrected Z-statistic maps and coordinate tables). Results are reported in figures/tables and participant/sample/MRI/preprocessing details are provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment of eligibility.

This study reports task-evoked fMRI BOLD responses to standardized visual affective stimuli and to pictures of alcoholic versus neutral beverages in alcohol-dependent participants. The methods and results describe within-participant contrasts to affective and alcohol-related images and group-level voxelwise activation differences (e.g., reduced insula activation and other clusters; referenced table S3 with coordinates), indicating whole-brain/small-volume-corrected voxelwise results are available. Participant and cue details are reported. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided here. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for visual cue-reactivity fMRI, within-participant cue>control contrasts, and group-level voxelwise reporting. Full text appears complete (supplementary tables are referenced but their absence does not preclude inclusion).

This study used visual opioid-related images (drug cues) in a drug-cue paradigm, so I3 is met. However, the reported analyses focus on multivariate dynamic measures (state engagement variability) and within-participant comparisons of SEV (cue vs rest), not on standard task-evoked voxelwise activation contrasts. The full text does not present a group-level voxelwise drug-cue>control contrast or provide coordinates/whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results (supplemental traditional activation analyses are only alluded to but not reported here). Therefore it fails I4 and I5. Exclusion criterion E4 applies because the paper reports non-standard dynamic/rest-related analyses without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result required for cue-reactivity meta-analysis. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol-associated pictures and IAPS affective (positive/negative/neutral) images, with within-subject contrasts (alcohol>neutral; positive>neutral; negative>neutral). Group-level voxelwise random-effects analyses are reported (2-sample and 1-sample t-tests) with voxelwise thresholds and coordinates presented in tables/figures, fulfilling the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI visual cue-reactivity studies and should be INCLUDED.

This study examines visual food-cue reactivity in women with bulimia nervosa and includes within-subject contrasts of food cues > neutral cues (satisfies I3 and I4) and reports participant demographics and MRI parameters (I7). However, all reported neuroimaging analyses are ROI-based (average ROI signal comparisons and paired t-tests), with no evidence in the main text of group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps reported as whole-brain or small-volume-corrected results. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or SVC-corrected result). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (qualifying whole-brain or SVC-corrected voxelwise result). I6 is not satisfied because no qualifying voxelwise results are available in tables/figures/supplement. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not report the required within-participant contrast of drug cues > control (I4 not met). It used visual alcohol cues (I3 met) and provides group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (e.g., win>lose contrast with coordinates and FDR correction) meeting I5, reports results in figures/tables (I6), and provides participant demographics and MRI/preprocessing details (I7). However, no voxelwise alcohol-cue > neutral/control contrast (with whole-brain or small-volume corrected coordinates) is presented in the main text, tables, or figures, so the primary inclusion criterion I4 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria from the list directly apply. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol cues (images) with a within-participant alcohol>control (ALC-H2O) contrast. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain results are reported (voxelwise Z=3.1, p<0.001; cluster-wise p<0.05) with tables/figures of significant clusters (VmPFC and other regions). Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, 7T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (fMRIPREP, FSL FEAT). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met.

This is an empirical human neuroimaging study of drug-cue reactivity using visual cues and within-subject contrasts; however, it used PET (H2^15O) rather than functional MRI. The review’s inclusion criterion I3 requires functional MRI. Although the study provides within-participant drug-cue>control contrasts (drug video vs neutral video) and reports group-level voxelwise SPM results (satisfying I4, I5, I6), it fails I3 (fMRI modality). No exclusion criteria E3–E6 are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded because it does not meet the modality-specific inclusion criterion (I3).

This randomized clinical trial includes an fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity task with task-evoked voxelwise results. The paper reports within-participant cue-induced activity (cue>control) contrasts (baseline vs week 26 reductions within the exenatide group) and group-level interaction effects. It also reports whole-brain voxelwise exploratory results (significant clusters in left caudate/septal area and right middle frontal gyrus) with supplemental appendices referenced for detailed coordinates. The methods/author contributions note adaptation of the fMRI ALCUE paradigm to E-Prime (implying visual cue presentation). Participant age/sex and cue type are reported. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not limited to ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses, and this is original human task fMRI data. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion); supplemental details are available. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is includable for the meta-analysis of visual reward-related cue-reactivity.

Exclusion E3 applies: the study reports only ROI-based analyses (extracting average beta values from a priori 4mm spheres and using these in Cox/logistic regressions) with no group-level whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise task-evoked statistical results presented. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI cue-reactivity using visual smoking images), I4 (within-participant contrast of smoking cues > neutral/control stimuli), and I7 (reports participant demographics and methodological details). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group-level result was reported). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded under E3.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of natural reward (visual food cues) reporting within-participant food>nonfood contrasts and group-level voxelwise results (figures and coordinates). The paper reports MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, SAS/SPSS), participant age/sex, and other relevant details. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (visual natural reward cue-reactivity, within-subject cue>control contrast, and qualifying group-level voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures).

This is a task-based fMRI study of smoking cue reactivity with visual cues and within-subject smoking>neutral contrasts, and reports participant demographics and MRI acquisition/processing details. However, the reported group-level analyses are ROI-averaged statistics (parameter estimates from 5-mm a priori spheres) rather than voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting) and does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (no qualifying group-level voxelwise whole-brain or SVC result reported). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual smoking cue reactivity), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I7 (reporting of age/sex, cue type, field strength, preprocessing software). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no qualifying voxelwise group-level result). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual smoking cues (images) and a within-subject contrast of smoking versus neutral images. Group-level voxelwise analyses were conducted (searchlight MVPA accuracy maps warped to MNI space, smoothed, and tested with nonparametric methods and cluster-wise correction for multiple comparisons), with results reported as significant clusters/regions. Participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, AFNI, FSL, Princeton MVPA toolbox) are reported. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This empirical fMRI study uses a monetary incentive delay (MID) task with clear visual cues signaling reward/loss (satisfies I3). It reports within-subject contrasts of reward anticipation versus non-incentive and gain versus non-gain outcomes (satisfies I4). Group-level voxelwise statistical maps are presented and reported with familywise correction (Monte Carlo simulation) and voxelwise t-tests (satisfies I5 and I6). Methods report participant ages/sex, cue types, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/software (AFNI) (satisfies I7). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so it appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity to natural (monetary) rewards with visual cues.

This is a task-based fMRI study using the Monetary Incentive Delay task with visual cues (large-reward cue vs. no-reward cue), providing a within-participant contrast of reward-cue>control. Voxel-wise group-level analyses (LME with TFCE and FWE correction) are reported with coordinates/tables and figures. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength variability, preprocessing and software details are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

The study is an fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity task using visual alcohol pictures (I3 met). It used a within-subject alcohol vs neutral design and conducted within-participant analyses (I4 met) and reports participant demographics, cue type, 3T MRI, and preprocessing/software (I7 met). However, the paper does not report any group-level voxelwise task-evoked activation results (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected). Instead, results are ROI-to-ROI PPI/seed-based connectivity analyses and ROI-based findings only. Therefore it violates exclusion criteria for connectivity/ROI-only studies (E4) and ROI-only reporting with no qualifying voxelwise result (E3). Inclusion criterion I5 (requirement for at least one qualifying voxelwise group-level task-evoked result) is not satisfied. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of smoking (drug) cue-reactivity using visual smoking-related images and neutral images. It includes within-subject contrasts (smoking > neutral) with subject-level beta maps and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked whole-brain random-effects analyses with cluster-level correction. Voxelwise results (regions, statistics, cluster-corrected thresholds) are reported in the main text and connectivity results are supplementary but do not replace the task-evoked contrasts. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and analysis software (BrainVoyager, GIFT), cue type (visual images), and participant sex. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (includes background, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of nicotine-deprived smokers that used visual cigarette cues (images of cigarettes) and neutral object images, with within-subject contrasts comparing cigarette cues to control (e.g., acquaintance+cigarette vs acquaintance+pen). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with cluster-level correction (Monte Carlo simulation, p<0.05 corrected) and peak coordinates/figures/ROI results are provided. Participant age/sex, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using audiovisual (multimodal including visual) smoking cues and a non-smoking control video, with within-subject contrasts of smoking cues > non-smoking cues. Group-level voxelwise results are reported (cluster-wise corrected whole-brain analyses showing mOFC and other clusters) using SPM8, and methodological details (participant age/sex, 3.0T MRI, preprocessing/statistical approach) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of natural reward (food) visual cue reactivity. It uses visual food images (high- vs low-caloric) meeting I3. It includes within-participant contrasts comparing high-caloric > low-caloric (separately in water and tea conditions) and interaction contrasts, meeting I4. Group-level voxelwise results are reported (exploratory whole-brain tests and ROI small-volume-corrected results; coordinates and FWE-corrected p-values reported), satisfying I5 and I6. Participant demographics, cue types, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are reported, meeting I7. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study with within-participant contrasts (alcohol>neutral, stress>neutral) and reports whole-brain voxelwise, cluster-corrected group-level results; participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are provided. However, the experimental cues were personalized auditory imagery scripts (audio/imagery), not visual stimuli. Inclusion criterion I3 requires a clear visual cue component (visual-only or multimodal including visual cues), which is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded from the visual cue-reactivity meta-analysis.

This study employed visual smoking cues and a within-participant smoking>neutral contrast (I3, I4). It performed whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reported uncorrected cue>neutral activations (figure described), and provided methodological details (3T scanner, BrainVoyager, male participants), satisfying I6 and I7. However, the critical cue-reactivity contrast did not yield any results that survived correction for multiple comparisons, and no whole-brain FDR-corrected or small-volume-corrected significant voxelwise task-evoked results are reported for the smoking>neutral contrast; therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly met beyond this failure to satisfy I5. Consequently the study is excluded because it lacks a qualifying corrected voxelwise cue-reactivity result (I5 not met) despite meeting I3, I4, I6 and I7.

This paper reports an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual methamphetamine cues in humans (non-treatment-seeking individuals with methamphetamine use disorder). It includes a within-subject drug-cue>control-cue contrast (Methamphetamine Cue>Control Cue) and reports whole-brain, cluster-corrected voxelwise results (Z-stat maps, cluster thresholds Z>2.3 and Z>1.96 with p<0.05) with coordinate tables and figures (supplementary tables/figures). Participant demographics (age, sex) and MRI details (3T Siemens Trio, preprocessing and FSL software) are provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of smoking (drug) cue reactivity using visual smoking cues (grayscale images). It used a within-subject CUE>neutral contrast (abstinence vs satiety sessions) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with multiple-comparison correction and cluster masking; coordinates/figures/tables are provided. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and analysis software (FSL), and participant age/sex. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical study). Therefore the article satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is an fMRI study of nondrug (monetary) reward cue-reactivity using clear visual cues (shape cues and word cues). The paper reports within-subject contrasts comparing reward-predictive cues versus non-incentive cues (pre-response reward anticipation: $1/$10 vs $0), post-response WIN vs HIT cue contrasts, and reward notification contrasts (wins vs non-wins). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps are reported (whole-brain analyses with FDR correction) and activation maxima are listed in tables/figures. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, 3dMEMA) are reported. Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This full text is an empirical fMRI study of favorite-food cue reactivity (natural reward) with whole-brain voxelwise results. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant contrasts for favorite-food cues vs control/other conditions are reported), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with correction are reported), I6 (voxelwise results are described and available in main/supplementary materials), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, field strength, and analysis software details reported). However, it fails I3: the cue modality is guided-imagery audiotapes (auditory/personalized imagery), not visual or multimodal designs that include visual cues. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study must be excluded because it does not include a clear visual cue component required by the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images) with a within-participant contrast of food>non-food. The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results (cluster-corrected, Z>2.3, p<.05) presented in figures and tables. Key details required by I7 are reported (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software (FSL)). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrast, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of nicotine-deprived smokers using visual cigarette cues and within-participant contrasts, but the reported analyses are primarily ROI-based (a priori anatomically defined ROIs and comparisons of mean beta coefficients). The paper does not report any group-level voxelwise whole-brain results or small-volume-corrected voxelwise statistical maps/coordinates needed for inclusion. Therefore it fails the requirement for at least one qualifying voxelwise (whole-brain or SVC) group-level task-evoked result.

This is an fMRI study of cigarette cue-reactivity using visual images (IAPS/ISIS/stock)—it includes within-subject contrasts of cue matching (smoking cues) versus neutral matching demonstrating cue-elicited effects, and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (cluster-corrected) with MNI coordinates (precuneus peak) and tables/figures. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (fMRIPrep, FSL). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

The full text reports only ROI-based analyses (mean BOLD across anatomically defined ROIs with repeated-measures ANOVAs) and does not present any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical results (no coordinate tables, voxelwise maps, or SVC results are reported). This violates exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting). The study does meet I3 (fMRI study with visual smoking cues), I4 (within-participant smoking>control contrasts were analyzed), and I7 (participant demographics and MRI/preprocessing details reported). It does not meet I5 (no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise result) and I6 (no qualifying voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study is an empirical BOLD-fMRI task study using visual natural reward (food) cues with within-subject food vs. non-food contrasts. It reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results (exploratory whole-brain FDR cluster-corrected analysis showing OFC and VS) and also provides ROI and coordinate-based results. Participant demographics, cue type, scanner details, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study is an empirical fMRI investigation of tobacco (drug) cue reactivity using visual smoking images, employing a within-subject smoking>neutral contrast and reporting group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (FSL FLAME1 cluster-thresholded; cluster information referenced). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are reported. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI task-evoked voxelwise results suitable for meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food images (natural rewards) and reports within-participant contrasts of interest (e.g., Look Craved > Look Neutral; Look Craved > Look Not Craved). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported with cluster-correction (AlphaSim) and coordinates for significant clusters; the paper also interrogates the small ventral striatum ROI with an appropriately reported voxel cluster. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12b, FSL) are reported. Thus it meets the meta-analysis objective and all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food images (natural reward cues) vs neutral images (AC>NC) with within-subject contrasts and group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses. The full text contains introduction, methods (3T MRI, task, preprocessing and whole-brain GLM), results reporting voxelwise clusters and statistics, and discussion, so it meets the meta-analysis requirements for visual cue-reactivity. No exclusion criteria apply.

The supplied full text is incomplete (only acknowledgments and references are provided); core article sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are missing so key methodological details cannot be verified. I cannot confirm whether this is an fMRI task with visual reward cues (I3), whether a within-participant cue>control contrast was reported (I4), or whether qualifying voxelwise group-level whole-brain or small-volume-corrected results were reported (I5/I6). Title suggests visual food-cue fMRI in PCOS patients, but that alone is insufficient. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I3, I4, I5, I6, I7.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (IAPS images paired with alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverage pictures). The study reports within-subject contrasts comparing alcoholic versus non-alcoholic beverage cues (both alcohol>non-alcohol and non-alcohol>alcohol contrasts) and provides group-level voxelwise statistical maps with family-wise error cluster correction and reported clusters/tables. Results are presented in figures/tables and VOI follow-ups; methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing steps, and analysis software (AFNI). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI task contrasts with qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results.

This empirical fMRI study uses visual smoking-related and affective images and reports within-subject contrasts (smoking>neutral, positive>neutral, negative>neutral) entered into group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM8). Results are reported voxelwise with coordinates and cluster statistics within an anatomical mask (small-volume approach) with cluster correction, fulfilling the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue types, scanner field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual fractal cues predicting non-alcohol monetary-like rewards (natural reward-related cues). The study reports within-subject parametric analyses of expected reward value (ERV) at cue/decision time and RPE at outcome time, and presents group-level voxelwise whole-brain FWE-corrected results with coordinates and statistics for within-group activations and between-group contrasts. Methods report participant demographics, cue type (visual fractals), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, only between-group without within-subject cue contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

The study is an fMRI investigation of cigarette (drug) cue-reactivity using visual smoking images and reports within-participant contrasts of smoking images versus nonsmoking/control images during non-neurofeedback runs. Group-level voxelwise random-effects paired t-tests (craving vs resistance / smoking vs nonsmoking) were performed and voxel clusters (P<0.05, cluster extent threshold) are reported in tables/figures. MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (visual drug cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results), I6 (results reported in tables/figures), and I7 (key methodological details provided). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-subject cue>control analyses, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of drug cue-reactivity using visual stimuli tailored to cocaine, alcohol, and cigarette users. It includes within-participant contrasts of drug cues > neutral control images and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with coordinates and cluster-level correction (voxelwise threshold and AFNI 3dClustSim cluster correction). Methods report MRI field strength, preprocessing and analysis software (SPM12, AFNI), participant demographics, and task details. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using a cocaine-word Stroop task (visual word cues). It includes a within-participant CW>NW (cocaine words vs neutral words) contrast used in analyses. The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (SPM second-level one-sample t-tests, cluster-defining thresholds and cluster-level p-values) used to localize activations, with results described in main text and supplementary materials. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12), participant demographics, and cue type are reported or referenced. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

Full text is complete and reports a task-evoked, group-level, voxelwise alcohol>control contrast with cluster-corrected whole-brain results (satisfies I4 and I5). Results are reported in tables/figures and preprocessing/statistical software are described (I6, I7). However, the cue modality is gustatory (taste cues: alcohol vs. litchi juice), not visual; the meta-analysis requires a clear visual cue component (I3). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criterion I3 (visual cue requirement) despite meeting I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (pictures) in alcohol-dependent patients and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with small-volume correction. The paper includes within-participant cue contrasts such as [alcohol pull > soft drink pull] with peak coordinates and FWE SVC-corrected p-values in mPFC (and SVC results in NAcc), reports MRI field strength (3 T), preprocessing and statistical software (SPM8), and participant characteristics (male alcohol-dependent inpatients). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking-related cues (ISIS images) in a within-subjects randomized crossover design. The authors report within-participant contrasts of smoking>neutral at the group level with voxelwise whole-brain results (uncorrected p<0.001, cluster threshold 10) and provide coordinates/tables and figures. MRI field strength (1.5T), stimuli, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. Participant sex/mean age are not fully reported (preferred per I7 but not required). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

Exclude because the experimental cue modality is individualized script-driven guided imagery (auditory/imaginal), not visual cues. The review requires studies with a clear visual cue component (I3), which this study does not provide. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant contrasts: alcohol cue > neutral-relaxing reported), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results with familywise correction), I6 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables), I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistics reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (visual cue component). Exclusion criteria met: none []. Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Exclusion E3 met: the study reports ROI-based analyses (extraction of COPEs from 14 a priori ROIs) and does not present group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate tables. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues – food images), I4 (within-participant contrast: food vs. object/baseline). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level voxelwise whole-brain or SVC results reported), I6 (no voxelwise coordinate tables/figures of qualifying results provided). I7: participant demographics, cue type, and software are reported though field strength is not explicitly stated (missing detail does not override exclusion). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study does not provide the required voxelwise task-evoked results for inclusion in the voxelwise meta-analysis.

This fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity meets several inclusion criteria for the review (I3: uses an alcohol visual cue-reactivity task; I4: reports within-participant ALC>BEV contrasts extracted per participant; I7: reports participant age/sex and necessary metadata). However, the neuroimaging analyses are ROI-based (mean ALC vs BEV percent signal change extracted from predefined ROIs) and the paper does not report any group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) or coordinate tables/voxelwise maps in the main text/supplement (no evidence of SVC/voxelwise results in the provided full text). Therefore it fails I5 and does not provide qualifying voxelwise results as permitted by I6, and it meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI analyses without qualifying voxelwise results). Conclusion: EXCLUDED.

This fMRI study examines appetitive (natural food) cue-reactivity using visual cues (pictures + tones paired with liquid food) and reports within-participant contrasts comparing CS+ > CS−. Group-level voxelwise results are reported with small-volume correction (amygdala, NAcc, vmPFC) at FWE-corrected thresholds, satisfying the requirement for a task-evoked voxelwise result. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, Matlab) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study is an empirical fMRI investigation of alcohol cue reactivity using visual alcohol and neutral images and reports within-participant contrasts between alcohol and neutral cue conditions. Group-level voxelwise analyses are described (voxel-wise one-sample t-tests, AFNI 3dttest++, cluster thresholds) with results presented in maps, tables, and supplementary materials. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (visual alcohol images), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus all inclusion criteria I3–I7 are met and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study using visual cigarette and food cues and reports group-level voxelwise (whole-brain and ROI-thresholded) task-evoked results; however, it does not present a within-participant cue>control (drug cues > neutral/control or natural reward cues > neutral/control) contrast. The analyses focus on regulation contrasts (LATER vs NOW) and cue type comparisons (cigarette vs food) but no drug-cue vs control-stimulus contrast or neutral baseline is reported. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 is not met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3, I5, I6, I7. No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study reports resting-state, seed-based functional connectivity (DLPFC seed) comparing alcohol dependence (AD) and internet gaming disorder (IGD) during abstinence; it does not implement a task-based cue-reactivity paradigm with visual cues nor a within-participant cue>control contrast. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (only seed-based connectivity/resting-state analyses without task-evoked results) and E5 (no within-participant cue>control contrasts; only between-group comparisons). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (no drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with clear visual cues), I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (no task-evoked whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results), I6 (no task-evoked voxelwise coordinates available). Full text appears complete. Consequently the study should be EXCLUDED from this meta-analysis.

This study examines visual food cues (natural rewards) with fMRI and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses, but it does not provide a within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control (non-reward) stimuli. All stimuli are high-calorie food pictures and contrasts are between cognitive-regulation conditions (up-regulation, suppression, reappraisal) and passive viewing of the same food cues rather than food>neutral or cue>non-cue contrasts. Therefore I4 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual food cues), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I6 (acceptable reporting formats), I7 (participant and MRI details reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4. No exclusion criteria from the list are directly triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical human fMRI study of smoking cue reactivity using visual stimuli (International Smoking Image Series). It reports within-subject contrasts (smoking cue > neutral cue) with whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses (FDR-corrected results) and provides coordinates/figures. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and analysis software (SPM8, FSL) and detailed methods are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This article is excluded because it does not report task-based fMRI voxelwise results for visual drug or natural reward cue-reactivity. The paper is a symposium summarizing human laboratory studies (IV alcohol self-administration, taste tests, HPA-axis measures, and clinical assessments) and while it briefly notes that an fMRI study investigated neural correlates of stress and alcohol-context cues, the full text provides no fMRI methods, no visual cue fMRI task description, and no within-participant drug-cue>control voxelwise results (whole-brain or SVC). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no functional MRI study assessing visual cue-reactivity), I4 (no within-participant cue>control fMRI contrast reported), I5 (no group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected results). Exclusion criteria met: none of the specified exclusion IDs (E3–E6) directly apply, but failure to meet required inclusion criteria leads to exclusion. Full text appears complete for the presented experiments (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study that uses visual smoking-related cues and neutral pictures during task fMRI and reports within-subject contrasts of smoking vs neutral cues. Group-level voxelwise results are reported (whole-brain 2×2 ANOVA with FWE correction and tables/figures of coordinates), satisfying voxelwise task-evoked reporting. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This study investigates fMRI responses to visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports within-participant contrasts (fattening > nonfattening), and it provides participant demographics and imaging/preprocessing details. However, the fMRI results are reported using ROI-based averages and ICCs across a priori ROIs rather than presenting any group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results (no coordinates or voxelwise SVC results are reported). Thus it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses). Inclusion IDs met: I3 (fMRI with visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I7 (reporting of age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistics). Inclusion ID not met: I5 (no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (high- and low-calorie images) as natural reward stimuli, with within-participant contrasts (high-calorie>objects; low-calorie>objects) and group-level voxelwise analyses. The authors report small-volume-corrected voxelwise results within a priori ROIs with FWE correction, and provide coordinates/psc extraction details. Methods report participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). Therefore all inclusion criteria for a visual-cue task-evoked voxelwise result are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports task-evoked BOLD fMRI responses to visual food cues (images of milkshake vs water) with within-participant contrasts (anticipatory milkshake cue > anticipatory tasteless-solution cue and receipt contrasts). Analyses were conducted as group-level voxelwise whole-brain tests (cluster-level q-FDR < 0.05) and report anatomical locations and peak coordinates. Methods report MRI field strength (Siemens Allegra 3T), preprocessing, and SPM12 software. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study does not assess drug or natural reward cue-reactivity using clear visual cues. The fMRI task is a real-time smoking decision paradigm with stress manipulations (working-memory load, shock probability) and in-scanner e-cigarette delivery, not a visual drug-cue>control stimulus contrast. Although the paper reports whole-brain analyses and provides participant/MRI details (I5, I6, I7 satisfied), it fails to meet I3 (visual cue-related drug/natural reward reactivity) and I4 (within-participant drug-cue>control or natural reward>control contrast). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual smoking-cue videos and matched control videos, with within-subject contrasts of smoking>control at first level and a group-level random-effects voxelwise analysis (FLAME) with permutation-based TFCE correction (P<0.05). Results are reported as whole-brain voxelwise activations (figures and supplementary table) and include participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (videos), MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL). The full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, so the article appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, lack of within-subject cue>control contrast, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This article is a non-empirical narrative review summarizing fMRI and MRS findings across multiple studies rather than reporting original human fMRI data. It does not present an original within-participant drug-cue>control (or natural reward>control) voxelwise group-level contrast, nor does it report primary whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical coordinates/results. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical paper). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not an original fMRI cue-reactivity study with visual cues), I4 (no within-participant cue>control analysis presented), I5 (no qualifying voxelwise group-level task-evoked result), I6 (no primary voxelwise coordinates/results available in this paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods describing review process, results, discussion, references).

This fMRI study examines natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images and an within-participant food>non-food contrast. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with small-volume correction are reported (randomise TFCE p<0.05) with MNI coordinates provided, and the main text describes whole analysis details (3T MRI, preprocessing via FSL/FEAT, participant age/sex, cue type). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity, within-subject cue>control contrast, and at least one qualifying voxelwise (small-volume-corrected) group-level result. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study using pictorial (visual) smoking cues and neutral controls, reporting within-subject contrasts comparing smoking versus neutral pictures (LCSP minus LCNP) and cue-exposure-corrected contrasts (LCSP minus PNSP). Group-level voxelwise second-level random-effects analyses are reported with stereotactic coordinates and Z-values (whole-brain voxelwise results reported at p<0.001 uncorrected). Imaging parameters (3T), preprocessing and analysis software (SPM5), and participant demographics are provided. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study uses visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results with preprocessing/statistics details. However, it does not include a within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli (e.g., food pictures > neutral/non-food images or baseline); the reported contrasts compare different task instructions (inhibition, imaginary eating, passive viewing) applied to the same food stimuli rather than cue versus control stimuli. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4. Full text appears complete.

This study reports an fMRI task using visual Pavlovian cues (colored lights predicting snack foods), satisfying natural reward-related visual cueing (I3). It includes within-subject contrasts of CS+ > CS− (general PIT) and specific PIT contrasts (I4). The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results (FWE-corrected, coordinates/tables provided and results archived on NeuroVault), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain/small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical results (I5, I6). Methods report participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12), meeting reporting preferences (I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical fMRI). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).
